blurb: On a record field, `@example` pins the field's own value, which exists only where the field has a base type. A field of a named type takes its value from that type, so an example on the field would have no effect and is refused. Put the `@example` on the named type's declaration, where `Val` reads it.
example:
type Code = String where Matches("[A-Z]{3}")
type Ticket = { code: Code where Matches("[A-Z]+") @example("ABC") }    // ✗ `Code` is a named type

type Code = String where Matches("[A-Z]{3}") @example("ABC")    // ✓ pin it on the type
type Ticket = { code: Code }
summary: An `@example` on a field whose type is a named type (it belongs on the named type).
